S33.01.note: The Sites page is the dashboard; Settings > Privacy > Shared links > Manage also has a second list named Published artifacts (apps/web/features/settings/sections/PublishedArtifactsSection.tsx) with Open, Copy, History and Unpublish.
steps: Click Sites in the sidebar.
Look at the list: one card per published site, with its name, its link, a visibility label and a More actions (⋯) button.
Click the ⋯ button on a card and check it offers Rename, Sharing and Unpublish.
Compare with Expected: the list shows each site's state and its actions.

S33.04.needs: a chat that runs on the cloud (not Local or BYOK); the Web panel refuses cloud publishing for Local, BYOK or unknown origins
S33.04.note: The refusal for Local, BYOK and unknown origins is stated in apps/web/app/features/artifacts/page.tsx.
steps: Click Sites in the sidebar, then click Create.
In the chat, ask AGI to build a small app or page, for example: build a page with a button that counts clicks. Wait for the artifact to appear in the side panel.
Click Publish in the artifact panel. If the panel is narrow, open the More (⋯) button and choose Publish.
Compare with Expected: the assistant built the app from your prompt, and a link now appears above the panel with a Copy link button.

S33.07.note: No separate preview deployment or preview URL found; searched 'preview URL', 'preview link' and 'preview deployment' in apps/web/features/chat/components/artifacts, apps/web/features/sites, apps/web/app/shared-artifact and apps/web/lib/services/published-artifact-service.ts. The Publish link (S33.10) is the nearest match.

S33.10.needs: a published site (see S33.04) and a private browser window
S33.10.note: The artifact panel also shows the link after Publish, in a bar with a Copy link button (apps/web/features/chat/components/artifacts/ArtifactPreview.tsx).
steps: Click Sites in the sidebar and click the name of a published site.
Open the Settings tab and find the URL section.
Click Copy link, then open a private browser window (not signed in) and paste the link.
Compare with Expected: the published site opens at its public address without signing in.
S33.10.where: Sidebar > Sites > open a site > Settings > URL > Copy link

S33.12.needs: a workspace; a second member account is needed to check that members can open it
S33.12.note: The artifact panel uses different wording for the same choice ('Everyone in this workspace (N)' in apps/web/features/chat/components/artifacts/ArtifactPreview.tsx); the signed-out check is a tester step, not a confirmed behaviour in the code.
steps: Click Sites in the sidebar.
On a site card, click the ⋯ button, then Sharing.
Choose Your workspace. If you belong to no workspace the option is greyed out with the text 'Join or create a workspace to share with its members only.'
Compare with Expected: with a workspace, the site is saved as workspace-only; open its link from a signed-out private window and check it does not open for a visitor outside the workspace.
S33.12.where: Sidebar > Sites > ⋯ on a site card > Sharing > Your workspace

labels.text: No model on your plan can answer this app right now.

S33.20.note: The allowance is checked on the server per request (managed usage reservation in artifact-runtime-service.ts) and has no screen; the message is the failure text for an unavailable model route, not an allowance counter.
steps: Open the public link of a published app that uses AI in a window.
Use the app's AI action.
Compare with Expected: the app answers. If no model is available for the request, the message 'No model on your plan can answer this app right now.' appears instead.
S33.20.where: Open the public link of a published app that uses AI, and use the app's own AI control

S33.23.needs: a published site with at least two publishes (republish it once after S33.04)
S33.23.note: Restore calls the server and then refreshes the site; the exact wording of the Live marker is 'Live'.
steps: Click Sites in the sidebar and click the name of a site that has been published more than once.
Open the Settings tab and scroll to the Versions section.
Click Restore on an older version (not the one marked Live).
Compare with Expected: the restored version is now marked Live and is the newest entry; the section says restoring republishes it as the newest.
S33.23.where: Sidebar > Sites > site name > Settings > Versions > Restore

S33.24.needs: a test site you can unpublish; this cannot be undone
S33.24.note: The same action is also at Sites > site name > Settings > Unpublish site; the confirm button text 'Unpublish' is in apps/web/features/sites/hooks/useSiteActions.ts.
steps: Click Sites in the sidebar.
On a test site card, click the ⋯ button, then Unpublish.
Read the confirmation dialog, which names the site and says the link stops working; click Unpublish to confirm or Cancel to stop.
Compare with Expected: a toast says the site was unpublished and the link no longer works; open the old link in a private window to check it is unavailable.
S33.24.where: Sidebar > Sites > ⋯ on a site card > Unpublish

S33.25.note: Whether Duplicate is listed in every layout was not confirmed from the code.
steps: Open a chat that has an artifact and open the artifact in the side panel.
Click the More (⋯) button in the panel.
Click Duplicate.
Compare with Expected: a toast says 'Duplicated. Edits here no longer touch the original.' Edit the copy and open the original to check it did not change.
S33.25.where: Chat > open an artifact in the side panel > More (⋯) > Duplicate

S33.26.note: The Download source item sits in the download menu for text artifacts; the exact condition under which the menu offers it was not fully traced.
steps: Open a text or code artifact in the side panel.
Click the Download icon in the panel.
Click Download source (.<language>), for example .py or .html.
Compare with Expected: a file with the raw source downloads; open it in a text editor to check it matches the artifact.
S33.26.where: Chat > open a text artifact in the side panel > Download > Download source

S33.28.note: The only report link on a published site is for infringement or impersonation; no general abuse button was found, and takedown is an admin route (apps/web/app/api/admin/takedown/route.ts).
steps: Copy a published site's link from Sites (Settings > URL > Copy link) and open it in a window.
Scroll to the bottom of the page.
Click Report infringement or impersonation.
Compare with Expected: the report page titled 'Report infringing or impersonating content' opens with the published page's address filled in.
S33.28.where: Open a published site's public link > scroll to the bottom > Report infringement or impersonation

labels.text: This name cannot be used because it violates the AGI Workforce usage policy.

S33.29.needs: a test site; do not use real or offensive content beyond what the policy check needs
S33.29.note: The rename path that reaches this check was not traced end to end; the refusal text is confirmed in the route, and review and takedown for a published page are operator-side only.
steps: Click Sites in the sidebar, then on a site card click the ⋯ button and Rename.
Type a name that breaks the usage policy and save.

Compare with Expected: the save is refused with 'This name cannot be used because it violates the AGI Workforce usage policy.' Other content moderation (review and takedown) has no screen for the visitor.
S33.29.where: Sidebar > Sites > ⋯ on a site card > Rename, then save a name that breaks the usage policy

S33.30.needs: a test site you can unpublish; this cannot be undone
S33.30.note: No separate 'Delete app' control was found; Unpublish is the only removal, its confirmation says visitor data is deleted (apps/web/features/sites/hooks/useSiteActions.ts), and whether the app record itself is removed was not confirmed.
steps: Click Sites in the sidebar and click a test site's name, then open the Data tab and note the Shared data and Personal data lists.
Go back, click the ⋯ button on the card, then Unpublish, and confirm.
Compare with Expected: the link stops working for everyone and the confirmation said visitor data is deleted; check the old link is unavailable.
S33.30.where: Sidebar > Sites > ⋯ on a site card > Unpublish
